page: Microsoft Azure F2ams_v7 is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance within the Famsv7 series, combining high core frequencies with an expanded memory allocation. The server runs on a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz, providing 2 physical cores and 2 virtual CPUs with a 1:1 core-to-thread topology. Cache provisioning includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. System memory totals 16.0 GB, yielding 8.0 GB per core. The instance includes no bundled local storage, operating as diskless compute that relies entirely on remote storage, and provides no GPU hardware. Supported instruction set extensions include AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, AVX512 BF16, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded performance driven by the 4.5 GHz AMD architecture. In single-core stress-ng tests, the instance achieved a score of 3566.79, placing it in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems. Compression and decompression tests reflect similar strengths, reaching 38.38 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip and 16.97 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3 decompression. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reached 51.35 GB/sec, while write operations measured 34.61 GB/sec. Conversely, overall multithreaded capacity is bounded by the two-core limit, reflected in an average stress-ng multicore score of 7105.98, a weak PassMark CPU score of 6457.97, and weak throughput in multithreaded bzip3 decompression at 33.49 GB/sec.

From an operational cost perspective, the instance provides high single-thread compute density combined with a memory-per-core ratio typically reserved for memory-focused tiers, avoiding the premium of larger multi-core footprints when parallel scale is unneeded. Tradeoffs include low overall aggregate throughput, a modest 5.18 GB/sec static web serving rate, weak medium-model LLM inference, and dependence on remote block volumes for local disk I/O. The Microsoft Azure F2ams_v7 is best suited for single-threaded data transformation jobs, compression pipelines, Redis in-memory caching nodes, and lightweight data ingestion tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure F2ams_v7 is a compute-optimized instance from the Famsv7 family, featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs on 2 physical AMD EPYC 9V45 cores running at 4.5 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the server pairs 16.0 GB of memory (8.0 GB per core) with 32 MB of L3 cache, supporting vector instructions such as AVX-512 and BF16. It contains no dedicated GPUs and does not bundle local disk storage. The high clock speed delivers top-tier single-core performance, demonstrated by top-decile benchmark results in single-threaded stress-ng execution and gzip compression. Parallel capacity remains constrained by the two-core ceiling, resulting in moderate overall multicore throughput. The hardware balance provides cost efficiency for workloads requiring substantial RAM per core alongside fast single-thread execution. It is suited for single-threaded batch processing, lightweight memory caching, compression tasks, and moderate computational pipelines.
